title: openai-compat: map tool schemas + stabilize tool_choice & tool message formatting
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Adds deterministic schema mapping between Redwood tool definitions and the OpenAI-compatible function schemas, clarifies and implements tool_choice semantics for assistant-driven tool selection, and standardizes tool->assistant message formatting for improved compatibility with OpenAI client expectations and downstream SDKs.

Motivation: Customers integrating Redwood's tool-calling via our OpenAI-compat layer reported inconsistencies when (a) tool parameter schemas used complex nested types, (b) the assistant attempted to select a tool via tool_choice but the downstream client runtime misinterpreted the intent, and (c) tool result messages were not consistently surfaced as assistant messages in streaming contexts. This caused integration bugs in our TS/Python SDKs and user apps.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces a schema-mapping layer that flattens and annotates Redwood tool parameter schemas into OpenAI function-like JSON Schema compatible structures. The mapping preserves type hints, required fields, enums, and adds clear fallback behavior for unsupported constructs (e.g. union types, deeply nested maps). 2) Implements the tool_choice signal semantics: the assistant can now emit a single message with role "tool_choice" and content referencing a tool id and an optional reason string; the compatibility layer will translate this into the expected choice structure for OpenAI clients and ensure no duplicate tool calls are made in streaming fallback scenarios. 3) Standardizes tool message formatting: tool responses are wrapped into assistant messages with a metadata header that contains tool_id, call_id, and schema_version to make replay and audit deterministic. The wrapper is compatible with streaming chunking — partial tool outputs are aggregated and re-emitted as stable assistant events. 4) Updates SDK mappings (TS and Python) to decode the wrapper into native tool response objects and to expose a small helper to reconstruct original tool outputs if needed. 5) Adds unit and e2e tests and small docs/upgrade note.

Checklist: - [x] Schema mapping implementation + unit tests - [x] tool_choice signal handling and de-dup logic - [x] message wrapper + streaming stability changes - [x] SDK decoders updated (TS/Python) - [x] e2e test with fanout + streaming - [x] Docs and release notes

Implementation notes and decisions: - For complex Redwood schema constructs (unions, tuple-like arrays, arbitrary-map types) we map to a permissive "object" with a descriptive "x-redwood-compat" vendor extension string to preserve intent for clients that understand it. This avoids silent validation errors while keeping the OpenAI-compatible contract. - tool_choice is implemented as a single assistant->system transitional signal. We intentionally keep it a single message to avoid race conditions with streaming token emission. When the assistant emits tool_choice, the compatibility layer pauses normal content streaming and surfaces an explicit choice event to the SDKs. - Tool message wrappers use a compact JSON header prefixed with a stable marker ("[redwood-tool-v1]") followed by the tool payload. The SDK decoder strips the header and verifies schema_version before passing payload to the user callback. - Backcompat: old clients that don't implement the header will see the raw tool output as a string; we document the change and provide the SDK helper to migrate.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: some clients tightly parse assistant content and may break on the wrapper header. Mitigation: wrapper is optional behind a compatibility flag controlled per-organization; default enabled for new orgs, opt-in for legacy. SDKs decode by default. - Risk: schema mapping may be lossy for very dynamic types. Mitigation: we log mapping warnings to the per-request debug trace and include the original schema in audit logs.

Related: ENG-4123 (schema mapping for tool calls), ENG-4198 (streaming tool stability), SUP-1284 (customer report), and several prior openai-compat PRs addressing function calling glue.

Testing: included unit tests for mapping edge cases, integration test that runs an end-to-end assistant -> tool choice -> tool call -> streaming tool response -> assistant finalization, and updated SDK tests to verify decoding of the wrapper header. CI: all checks passed after one flaky lint fix (see CI notes).

review_comments: Ben Carter: Left a couple of questions about the vendor extension naming and whether we should use JSON-LD style context instead. Also asked to add a short example in the schema_mapper tests.
Aisha Kapoor: Responded that JSON-LD is heavier than we want for the compat shim; added x-redwood-compat with example in tests (see commit a1f4b2c).
Marta Ruiz: Noted that tool_choice signals should be idempotent for retries; requested explicit call_id propagation across retries.
Aisha Kapoor: Added call_id propagation and added e2e test to cover a retry scenario (commit d9a2e88).
Liam O'Connor: Verified streaming changes and asked for a comment in the wrapper implementation about partial-chunk aggregation semantics. A comment was added and test updated.
release_notes: OpenAI compatibility: improved function/tool calling compatibility by adding schema mapping for tool parameters, introducing stable tool_choice semantics to avoid duplicate calls in streaming scenarios, and standardizing tool message formatting for reliable SDK decoding. Includes SDK updates (TS/Python) and migration notes.
notes_for_release: Enable wrapper by default for new orgs; legacy orgs can opt-in. See docs/openai_compat/tool_calling.md for migration steps and SDK helpers.
